title: Plan a flight
body: Every flight starts on Today. Tap Plan new flight.

title: The flight
body: Here you choose the departure, the destination, any stops, the day and the aircraft. For this dry run the route is ready: your aerodrome, two turning points and back. A flight planned for another day gets a reminder the day before. Tap Create flight.

title: One page per flight
body: Each flight has its own page, from the plan to the logbook: the flight thread. Its four chapters (Plan, Prepare, Fly and Close) follow the stages of every flight; those with something to do now are open, the others are one line. The line under the title says when you leave and what is left.

title: What is left
body: What is left is always in the line under the title, and on Today. A tap on an item takes you to it.

title: START FLIGHT
body: START FLIGHT, in the Fly chapter, opens the Cockpit. For this dry run, the rest of Plan and Prepare has been ticked for you. In a real flight, START FLIGHT first lists anything still open.

title: Your first flight, on the ground
body: This is the Cockpit, opened by START FLIGHT. The aircraft waits for you at each step.

title: Check an item
body: CHECK ticks off the highlighted item and moves to the next one. Tap it once.

title: ENGINE START
body: Tap it once the engine is running: the app records the time, and the flight times start from there.

title: Defer an item
body: Can't do an item right now? DEFER puts it aside, and the app keeps it for later. Try it now.

title: Nothing is lost
body: Everything you deferred waits here, in amber. Tap it at any time to finish it.

title: READY FOR LINE UP
body: Tap it. The app uses this moment as the take-off time and times the route from it.

title: Watch the take-off
body: Open MAP. In a dry run, the aircraft lines up and takes off automatically; your next step is the climb check, once airborne.

title: Take-off detected
body: AéroCheck noticed the take-off and noted its time for the logbook. It does the same for go-arounds, touch-and-goes and full-stop landings, so you can focus on flying the plane.

title: Where you'll be
body: The blue line ahead of the aircraft shows where you'll be in 1, 2 and 5 minutes, at this speed and on this track.

title: What you read
body: GS, ALT and TRK come from the GPS. Below them, you find where the current leg leads and when you get there, then who to call: NOW and NEXT.

title: Changed frequency? Tap NEXT
body: NEXT is outlined: it is time to change to it, and the line along its foot runs out where the app changes by itself. When you change frequency, tap NEXT (on a phone, the NOW line) and it becomes NOW. Undo takes it back.

title: The turning point
body: The app detected the passage of this turning point: it recorded the time over on ROUTE and moved to the next leg automatically. If that was too early, Undo here takes it back.

title: Try a go-around
body: On this final, choose GO AROUND on the card: the aircraft climbs away and the app detects the go-around. In a real flight, you fly it yourself.

title: Go-around detected
body: The app detected the go-around and recorded it automatically: the checks went back to the climb check. If it wasn't one, Undo takes it back for a few seconds. After a real flight, you confirm it in the Flight review.

title: This time, a full stop
body: FULL STOP is already selected, so the aircraft lands. On short final, tap the landing check and work through its items.

title: ENGINE SHUTDOWN
body: The engine has stopped: tap it, and the app records the time.

title: END FLIGHT
body: It closes the flight and creates its logbook entry, with the times from the GPS track. This is a dry run, so none of it is kept.

title: After the flight
body: END FLIGHT moved the flight to CLOSE-OUT: the page now opens on Close, and the line under the title counts what is left. If you had filed a flight plan, closing it would come first, in red, with the number to call.

title: Logbook & costs
body: Block and flight time, the landings, the engine hours, and the cost at the aircraft's rate. Copy line puts the line on the clipboard. Close the sheet when you have read it.

title: Finish
body: Finish closes the flight's page; the flight stays in your logbook.

title: The year at a glance
body: Your hours, flights and landings, the hours per aircraft, what you spent and how your checks went. The dry run's logbook has five made-up flights before yours.

title: The flight's page
body: Everything about this flight is here: its track on the map, the altitude and speed chart (slide along it to replay the flight), the timeline, how each check ended, the engine hours and the plan compared with what you flew. Have a look around, then tap Next.
